newsitem.title: ITALY: Eni opens more than two pct up in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Eni opens more than two pct up in Milan.

text.p: Italian state-controlled energy group ENI opened 2.39 percent up at 9,800 lire per share in Milan after the end of its public share offer (OPV) on Friday.

The share offer, which was the third in the Eni privatisation process, was three times oversubscribed with some 830,000 Italian retail investors signing up for shares and huge interest from institutional investors around the world.
Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi hailed the operation as an extraordinary success and said the Treasury now expected to reduce its holding in Eni to 51.5 percent from 69.1 percent.
It had originally intended to cut its stake to 54.6 percent but given the demand, additional stock will be offered to the institutions under a so-called greenshoe option.
The Eni sale price was pegged at 9,288 lire per share for the small retail investors, while institutional investors will pay 9,575 lire -- Eni's closing price on the Milan bourse on Friday.
